A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Dendritic Localized Learning work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching the renumbered experimental settings and limitations.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-classification, character-prediction and time-series experiments, including comparative results, ablations and sensitivity analyses in Tables 1–3 and Figure 3.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds image and text classification results, resource measurements and a depth study in Tables 4–7.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain the compartment model, local-error computation, loss and forward/backward weight updates. Appendix B retains the final RNN update rules. The additional CNN/TextCNN evaluations do not document a change to DLL's procedure.

E1.justification: v2 retains the original datasets and adds CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet image classification, plus Subj and Movie Review text classification in Appendices E–F. This substantially broadens image coverage and adds a language task distinct from the existing character prediction.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their comparator membership. The new benchmark and resource comparisons reuse backpropagation. Newly discussed methods such as BurstProp, SoftHebb and Counter-current Learning are not added to the reported experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: Existing settings are retained, while Appendices E–H add several evaluation designs: four- and five-convolutional-layer CNNs without batch normalization or residual connections, TextCNN classification, CPU timing and GPU-memory measurements, and a three-architecture MNIST depth comparison. The added image benchmarks use CIFAR-100 accuracy and Tiny-ImageNet error rate. These are additional protocols, not revisions to the original experiments.

E4.justification: Tables 6–7 add a limited resource-overhead comparison and MNIST depth study, testing computational costs and architectural scaling. The existing backward-weight ablation and learning-rate/sequence-length sensitivity analyses in Table 3 and Figure 3 remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 1 still reports averages over four random seeds and Table 2 over three, with unchanged uncertainty summaries. The new appendix tables provide point estimates without adding run counts, seed information, uncertainty estimates or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Original results are retained, but Tables 4–7 add substantial evidence. DLL obtains 38.60% CIFAR-100 accuracy versus BP's 44.50%, and 82.90% Tiny-ImageNet error versus 78.60%. DLL-TextCNN achieves 84.40% on Subj and 70.79% on MR. Additional results show higher DLL resource use and MNIST accuracy ranging from 71.15% to 97.57% across tested depths.

T1.justification: Appendix B, Equation (15), replaces differentiation of losses at only the current and next time steps with an explicit sum over all remaining time steps and a chain-rule decomposition. This revises the derivation while preserving its final update expression. New Appendix C supplies qualitative convergence discussion, not a formal proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the claims that DLL satisfies three biological-plausibility criteria, performs strongly among qualifying alternatives, and trains MLPs, CNNs and RNNs. The additional experiments do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: New Appendix C explains convergence qualitatively and acknowledges the difficulty of formal proofs. Appendix G attributes additional resource costs to updating both weight sets and explicitly prioritizes biological plausibility over efficiency. The original SNN and unsigned-error limitations remain in Appendix I.

D1.justification: Reported code access changes from supplementary code with a planned public release to an explicit GitHub availability statement and URL. New appendices specify CNN channel configurations, TextCNN architecture provenance and CPU timing. Original implementation details and hyperparameters move unchanged from Appendix C to Appendix D.

R1.justification: Section 5 replaces its detailed target-propagation and predictive-coding contrasts with expanded positioning against segregated-dendrite work, Bartunov et al., BurstProp, SoftHebb and Counter-current Learning. Additional references broaden feedback-alignment and predictive-coding coverage and document the new TextCNN experiments, substantially revising the discussion of related approaches.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include rewriting Related Work, localized grammar and terminology corrections, additional appendix sections and cross-references, removal of the standalone reproducibility statement, and updated affiliation and conference text.

P2.justification: v2 adds four compact appendix tables for benchmark results, resource use and depth. Figures 1–3 and Tables 1–3 preserve their visual content. Other changes chiefly involve table placement and page or column reflow within the existing format.

improvement.justification: v2 broadens empirical support through additional image and text tasks, exposes previously unreported computational costs, and improves the RNN derivation and code-access documentation. These are useful gains over v1. Their impact is limited by the new comparisons using only backpropagation, incomplete protocol and uncertainty reporting for the added results, and convergence remaining qualitative rather than formally established.
